- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > history peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +20% above recent high or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) or shows strong bearish signals, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid early sell-off.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast deviates >5% from 30-day moving average, adjust toward average with decay factor (e.g., 0.85).
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.7, apply 10% weight to recent 7-day average; if <0.3, apply 15% weight to 30-day average.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to account for delayed reaction.
